title: Generator functions
learningObjectives: Explain generator functions and use JavaScript collections and iteration safely.

understand.concept: Generator functions use function* and yield to produce values lazily. Calling a generator function returns an iterator; each next() resumes execution until the next yield or completion. return() can end the generator early, and generators can be used to create custom iterables.
understand.whyItMatters: Generators are useful for sequences that are computed on demand and for expressing step-by-step iteration. They do not make a synchronous generator asynchronous; async generators are a separate feature.
understand.analogy: A generator is a dispenser that pauses after each item until the caller asks for the next one.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; collection identity, iteration, and binary storage follow JavaScript specification rules.

explain.narrative: The loop requests each value from the generator until it is complete.

examples.explanation: The loop requests each value from the generator until it is complete.

practise.guidedTask: Create a generator for page numbers. Stop it early with return() and compare lazy generation with building an array first.
practise.independentTask: Choose an appropriate collection or iteration technique for a small data task. Test duplicates, ordering, identity, and copying behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates its receiver.
Remember that object equality is based on identity.
Use typed arrays only when binary data semantics are needed.

questions.prompt: Which keyword pauses a generator and provides a value to its caller?
questions.explanation: yield suspends the generator and provides a value through the iterator protocol.
